text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT created — metering service reporting 'sample rate degradation' affecting token counting. Pager routed to @oncall-sre. Auto-tags: billing, metering, customer-impact. :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: Acked. I'm looking at the meter-emitter dashboards now.
oncall-sre: Early signal: token_delta stream shows ~7-12% undercount for a subset of EU customers since 03:05 UTC.
alex_chang: Repro run locally against latest emitter commit? I spun up a small replay and see gaps in sample windowing around sequence_id ranges 4.1e6-4.1e7.
maya_k: Copy — attaching a quick query: ```sql
SELECT window_start, count(*) FROM token_samples WHERE window_start >= '2026-03-17T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY window_start ORDER BY window_start LIMIT 8;
-- output: windows 03:00..03:12 show 8k, 7.2k, 6.5k, 6.4k, 8.1k, 8.0k, 7.9k, 7.8k
```
billing_team: Observed consequences: our overage-flagging rule has tripped for ~14 customers (false positives) because emitted counts dipped in some windows while shadow counters used later rebalance. We need quick mitigation.
sam_cs: Heads-up — two customers already opened support tickets citing unexpected overage alerts. No billing charges posted yet but emails went out.
oncall-sre: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Pin routing to stable emitter-v2 (rollback candidate) 2) Pause aggressive overage notifications for affected cohort 3) Start a small backfill job to recompute counts for last 6 windows.
ops_lead: Agreed. Oncall, can you push the routing pin and flip the notification flag? I can coordinate backfill.
oncall-sre: Doing step 1 now: rolling pin -> emitter-stable (command: `infractl route set emitter=emitter-stable --scope=eu-prod --dry-run=false`)
oncall-sre: Done. Confirmed new requests hitting emitter-stable in eu-prod (trace ids 0x9a3..0x9f2). Metrics show per-window counts trending back up after 2 windows.
maya_k: Backfill job scheduled: `backfill-meter --start 2026-03-17T02:54:00Z --end 2026-03-17T03:18:00Z --cohort=eu-shadow` — running on batch workers (ETA ~ 8m).
billing_team: Paused outbound overage emails for cohort eu-shadow via feature-flag (ff billing.overage.notify=off for tag eu-shadow). Confirmed no new emails will be sent.
sam_cs: I'll reply to the two tickets with a short explanation and ETA for resolution.
oncall-sre: Observability note: KV cache TTL behavior in emitter-v3 seems to have regressed under skewed sequence ingestion. We're opening a follow-up bug for v3 and scheduling a patch.
ops_lead: Customer impact: temporary false-positive overage alerts for ~14 customers, ~2 support tickets, no billed charges posted. Root cause suspected: sampler window boundary regression in emitter-v3 under bursty replay.
alex_chang: Adding logs snippet where the drop occurs: ```json
{"seq":41001234,"window":162,"emitter":"v3","sampled":false}
{"seq":41001235,"window":162,"emitter":"v3","sampled":false}
{"seq":41001236,"window":163,"emitter":"v3","sampled":true}
``` — indicates mis-assignment around boundary.
billing_team: Will validate backfill results and reconcile charges once counts are recomputed. If recon shows no net token shortfall, we'll retract the overage flags.
oncall-sre: Backfill finished. Recomputed windows show counts restored to expected baseline; difference reconciled. Rolling status to resolved for active mitigation.
ops_lead: Oncall handoff: @maya_k will own the postmortem and patch for emitter-v3, @alex_chang to file the regression PR, billing_team to run final reconciliation and customer outreach.
maya_k: Acknowledged — I'll start the postmortem draft and include timeline, mitigations, and customer comms draft.
sam_cs: I'll update customers with: "We identified a transient counting anomaly affecting a small set of customers. We have recomputed usage and confirmed no billed overcharges. We're following up with a detailed incident report."
oncall-sre: Marking incident as mitigated. Leaving monitoring on for 2 hours. If no regressions, we'll close the incident. :white_check_mark:
